messages:
devin: FYI we're seeing a consistent tiny-batch latency oscillation on quantized 4-bit models after the CUDA/driver roll to 12.9 yesterday :grimacing:
anya: saw that in canary too, small batches (1-4 tokens) spike ~2-3x intermittently? :eyes:
sam: confirmed on a100 and h100 in staging, looks like kernel selector is flipping between two kernels during the same sequence of requests
jen: quick profile dump — the dispatch changed to a generic matmul kernel for small N, which has worse setup overhead. snippet from perf trace:
```
[trace] batch=1 seq=8 profile: matmul_small_n 0.9ms -> matmul_generic 3.2ms
[trace] same callsite different kernel id: 0x1a -> 0x4f
```
devin: that explains it. this started right after driver + cuBLAS minor bump (driver 550.x -> 557.x + CUDA 12.9). CI uses 12.9 images now, which is why nightly perf checks caught it as a regression
ci-bot: nightly-e2e-smallbatch: latency regression at commit c3f9d2a (12% p95 increase) - artifacts: https://ci.redwood-internal/reports/2133040000
anya: I ran a quick bisect across our local triton autotune table snapshots. culprit looks like a change in Triton's heuristic for matmul kernel selection that now prefers generic when cuBLAS reports certain workspace sizes on 12.9
sam: also seeing KV cache prefetch hit rate drop slightly when the kernel path flips — more thread wakeups and extra memcpy ops
jen: small repro harness attached in the CI artifacts: run `./bench_smallseq --model tiny-quant --batch 1 --seq 16` and watch `nvprof` traces
ops-bot: rollout: dedicated/pool-2 canary paused due to latency SLO breaches; automatic rollback disabled (manual hold)
devin: plan: 1) pin kernel selector to previous heuristic in runtime as feature-flag for canary, 2) open Triton issue and test a fix, 3) coordinate with infra to hold CUDA 12.9 rollout until mitigations in place
anya: I can push a short-lived env var `REDWOOD_FORCE_LEGACY_MATMUL=1` to canary nodes, will that be quick to test?
sam: yes, we already have a toggle. patch + canary redeploy will take ~20min to validate. I can do that now
jen: if we need a faster stopgap we can also set `TRITON_DISABLE_AUTOTUNE=1` per-model but that may hurt throughput for large batches
devin: okay do the env-toggle on canary, gather p95 traces, then decide whether to revert the driver bump or apply runtime heuristic override
ci-bot: note: perf alert also flagged an increase in memcpy activity (host->device) at smallseq workloads, correlates with kernel change
anya: i've scheduled a quick triage in 30m, invite: @sam @jen @devin. will post results here. :thumbsup:
devin: thanks — leaving canary paused until we have numbers. if the env toggle fixes p95 I'll push a short PR to gate it behind a config and roll to prod canaries
jen: filing issue: https://github.com/triton-inference-server/issues/9999 (draft) with traces and kernel ids
sam: after we verify, we should add a small-batch regression test to CI that runs quant tiny-quant with batch=1/seq<=32 on CUDA 12.9 images to prevent recurrence
devin: agreed. also note for release notes: CUDA 12.9 may change kernel preference heuristics, recommend testing small-batch quant workloads before upgrade
ops-bot: incident-note: rollback not performed; mitigation in progress. will update when canary data available
anya: update (10m): env toggle applied to canary — immediate p95 improvement back to baseline. collecting traces now
devin: sweet. next steps: PR to make toggle available as runtime config, follow up with Triton/cuBLAS maintainers, and add CI regression test. closing hold if canary stays stable over 1hr
jen: linking the trace dump: https://artifacts.redwood/trace/2133050000.tgz
ci-bot: nightly-e2e-smallbatch: follow-up run shows 1.1% p95 delta (within noise)
devin: great work everyone, let's keep this thread for postmortem notes and put a short blurb in eng-releases that tiny-batch quant workloads were sensitive to CUDA 12.9 kernel selection heuristics.
